category_title: Students with LD who use prior knowledge or memory to predict future story events
minimal_context: The student is participating in a small reading group and anticipating future events in the book 'The Mouse and the Motorcycle'.
dialogue:
TUTOR: We are about to read the next part of 'The Mouse and the Motorcycle'. What do you want to find out in the text we are about to read?

STUDENT: Does Ralph have a sister that is going to lose—I mean a brother that is going to try and ride the motorcycle and then ()

TUTOR: So usually when we predict, we predict off of what we read so far. Where is that prediction coming from?

STUDENT: Well, in third grade my teacher read the book to the class.

TUTOR: I see. But what can we predict based on what we have read together?

STUDENT: I don't know... it was just a silly prediction.

options.A: Ask the student how she will respond to the author or what other sources of evidence might contribute to her understanding of the text.
options.B: Provide a break card kept on the desk as a prompt, allowing the student to ask for a break when needed by holding it up.
options.C: Withhold attention from the student when she engages in problem behavior during the reading group, providing no response to her off-task comments.
options.D: Allow the student to select a positive reinforcer before beginning the reading activity, which she earns when she finishes her work or makes an honest attempt.
